headline: On last trading day, Sensex crashed 1,000 points as foreign investors sold en-masse, wiping out ₹9.5 lakh crore.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed for trading today due to an NSE holiday. It will reopen on Monday, 5 October.

why: En-masse selling by foreign investors (FIIs) triggered a massive market downturn
Global concerns regarding high oil prices and potential interest rate hikes
Surging US Treasury yields impacting global investor sentiment
Technical pressure as benchmark indices recorded their longest weekly losing run in 25 years
whatHappening: INOX Group scions have filed for two separate IPOs worth ₹10,000 crore each
Government has capped sugar stock limits for dealers at 1,000 quintals for the festive season
Nayara Energy clarified that no fuel supply restrictions have been imposed across its retail network
India's food market has reached $600 billion, growing at a 7% CAGR with a focus on processing
summary: The Indian market is closed today for a holiday following a session where the Sensex crashed 1,000 points and Nifty slipped below 22,300. Foreign investor selling wiped out approximately ₹9.5 lakh crore in wealth as indices hit their longest weekly losing streak in decades. Amidst the volatility, INOX Group announced major IPO plans while the government tightened sugar stock limits for the festive season.
